items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. (1) The tier-4 fact is real and is used as evidence: WEB sets an opening curly quotation mark inside web:Ps.118.15 before its second sentence and the closing mark at the end of web:Ps.118.16; the row's observed_substrate_signals #2 offers that quotation-mark structure as a substrate signal with an absence arm ('the voice of rejoicing (v15a) itself carries no quotation mark'), the driver field labels the unit 'A quoted acclamation', and strongest_rejected_alternative rejects the v16 cut as 'what vv15-16 just quoted as communal acclamation' - translation punctuation doing corroboration work and counterevidence-by-absence, barred by the campaign addendum (E-23). (2) It is corroboration, not the resting point, so medium is the right band: the voice contrast stands in the MT bytes with no punctuation layer - oshb:Ps.118.17 carries three 1cs prefix forms, אָמ֥וּת, אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה, וַ֝אֲסַפֵּ֗ר (byte tier, word indices 1, 3, 4), and oshb:Ps.118.18 two 1cs object suffixes, יִסְּרַ֣נִּי, נְתָנָֽנִי (byte tier), while oshb:Ps.118.15 and oshb:Ps.118.16 carry no first-person form at all; the 'acclamation' reading itself is derivable from oshb:Ps.118.15's own syntax, where ק֤וֹל רִנָּ֬ה וִֽישׁוּעָ֗ה בְּאָהֳלֵ֥י צַדִּיקִ֑ים (byte tier) names a voice and the nominal clause יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל follows as its content. The row's byte claim re-collates: that four-token run stands byte-identically at oshb:Ps.118.15 (word indices 5-8) and oshb:Ps.118.16 (word indices 3-6), and a byte sweep of the run returns exactly those 2 verses. (3) BOTH SIDES of the rival seam at 118:16|118:17 weighed under the book's rules: the preceding unit would close on the doubled clause יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל (second occurrence, oshb:Ps.118.16, byte tier) - a refrain-type close - and the following unit would open לֹֽא אָמ֥וּת (oshb:Ps.118.17, byte tier) on a speaker return to the first person; both are ruled-class signals, so the rival is live on bytes and the row's rejection of it must rest on the byte-grounded voice contrast and on v17 answering vv15-16, never on the quotation marks - which is why the tier-4 lean is a defect and not a stray remark. The row's own edges are sound on ruled classes from both sides: oshb:Ps.118.14 closes in the first person (וַֽיְהִי לִ֝֗י לִֽישׁוּעָֽה, byte tier) and oshb:Ps.118.15 opens on the unaddressed communal scene; oshb:Ps.118.18 closes in the first person (נְתָנָֽנִי) and oshb:Ps.118.19 opens on the 2mp imperative פִּתְחוּ (byte tier), coherent with M8-Ps-395 and M8-Ps-397. Ps 118 is an identity psalm (crosswalk); no selah and no K/Q in MT 118:15-18 (pmarks; paseq count-only, 1 at MT 118:15, inventory-cited, single-witness, no seam role); all three Hebrew runs in the row reproduce byte-for-byte in the staged extract. (4) Repair validated: the proposed re-grounding on the 1cs distribution is byte-sound and ENDORSED as a field repair (no respan), with two qualifications - name all three v17 forms (the proposal names two) and phrase 'communal' as the row's reading of the voice-clause syntax rather than a byte fact; the WEB quotation mark may remain only as an explicit tier-4 non-evidential disclosure. Verdict: confirm at medium; span_change false, so span_ruling n/a.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Three interpretive declarations follow the preceding scene: אֶ֭בֶן מָאֲס֣וּ הַבּוֹנִ֑ים הָ֝יְתָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ פִּנָּֽה (oshb:Ps.118.22) (“The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.” web:Ps.118.22), “This is Yahweh's doing. It is marvelous in our eyes” (web:Ps.118.23 = oshb:Ps.118.23, whose Hebrew demonstrative זֹּ֑את sits at word index 3, not the verse-initial position its English rendering suggests), together with “This is the day that Yahweh has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!” (web:Ps.118.24 = oshb:Ps.118.24, the row's only genuinely verse-initial demonstrative, זֶה) -- a triad of interpretive sayings rather than the antiphonal request-and-reply shape of the gate scene at 118:19-21. The verse-initial demonstrative device itself is not what unites the triad -- a book-wide sweep finds it only at 118:20 and 118:24, so it actually straddles this row's own opening seam at 118:21|118:22 (118:20 sits in the preceding row) rather than running through all three of this row's verses. The triad's own unity rests on its shared interpretive-declaration shape and its position after the gate liturgy, not on a verse-initial demonstrative.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A final personal declaration -- אֵלִ֣י אַתָּ֣ה וְאוֹדֶ֑ךָּ ("my God, you, and I will thank you") and אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אֲרוֹמְמֶֽךָּ ("my God, I will exalt you") (oshb:Ps.118.28, web:Ps.118.28 “You are my God, and I will give thanks to you. You are my God, I will exalt you.”) -- names God with two distinct Hebrew words (אֵלִ֣י, אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י) that WEB renders identically as "You are my God," the doubling a rendering effect rather than a repeated Hebrew lexeme -- closes the psalm with its opening line repeated verbatim: הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.118.29) is byte-identical (collate.py, byte tier) to הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.118.1), a true hodu inclusio framing all 29 verses of the psalm.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v29 as belonging with the altar procession at 118:25-27 would merge the closing inclusio into festal-procession texture; the word-for-word repetition of v1 (7 words) instead marks v29 as the psalm's deliberate frame-closing verse.
